method.diagnostic: A descriptive held equal-alarm comparison counts the most useful edits reachable with each observed rule and each false-group budget. Held points never enter the frozen decision.
method.focus: Use existing native sentence positions and both immediate neighbors. Require 12–65 lexical words in each of the three sentences, 50 lexical words elsewhere, and six distinct content terms in each sentence.
method.joint: Take the smaller positive departure on the two unit scales. Inspect the ablations independently.
method.metric: Require at least half of the exact edited non-whitespace characters and .30 intersection over union. Keep ordinary same-work substitutions as controls and count false alerts by source group.
method.novelty: Against the same remaining article vocabulary, count the share of each sentence's unique content terms absent from the remainder. Score the excess over the more novel neighbor. Content terms have four or more characters and exclude the fixed function words.
method.point: Select at most one uniquely highest positive focus per document. Each arm uses the third highest genuine source-group maximum in the older technical selection partition, with strict excess.
method.richness: Compare the fraction of distinct types expected in a uniform sample of 12 lexical words without replacement. Score the focus distance outside the two-neighbor range, in either direction.
method.transfer: Against current plus each supplement, report new useful groups, added genuine groups, wrong-only locations and measured scope separately for later Kubernetes and eLife works. The joint arm must add useful cases from both generator families in each held panel with no more than one extra genuine group in either panel.
